items.fromString:
h3. User story

As a user of GCP Dedicated, when I need to choose storage for block workloads, I want the default storage class to be Hyperdisk Balanced so that I use only supported storage options.

As a user of GCP Dedicated, when I create storage resources, I want the platform to use the supported storage constraints so that I avoid unsupported disk and storage types.

h3. Context

GCP Dedicated supports Hyperdisk Balanced only for block storage.  
This applies to all services.

For object storage, Cloud Storage is available only in a single region.  
A bucket location must be set explicitly.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Default SC on GCP Dedicated is Hyperdisk Balanced.
* Compute Engine VMs can only attach Hyperdisk Balanced volumes.
* GKE uses Hyperdisk Balanced as the only storage class for PVCs.
* There is no fallback to Persistent Disk in GKE.
* Cloud SQL supports Hyperdisk Balanced and Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability only.
* Cloud SQL has no data cache.
* Cloud Storage is available only in a single region.
* Dual-region and multi-region storage classes are not available.
* Legacy storage classes are unavailable:
** Multi-Regional
** Regional
** DRA
* Standard storage classes are available within the single region:
** Standard
** Nearline
** Coldline
** Archive
* Bucket location must be set explicitly.
* There is no default bucket location.
* Domain-named buckets are not available.
* Storage Transfer Service is not available.
* Storage Insights is not available.
* HMAC keys must use service accounts, not user accounts.
* The following are not available:
** Persistent Disk of any type
** Local SSD
** Hyperdisk Extreme
** Hyperdisk Throughput
** Filestore
** Parallelstore
** Multi-region buckets
** Dual-region buckets
** Memorystore Redis
** Memorystore Memcached

h3. Other information

* Block Storage supports Hyperdisk Balanced only.
* Cloud Storage is available with these constraints.
* In short: Hyperdisk Balanced for block storage, single-region Cloud Storage for object storage.

*Description:*

  The KEP template's Production Readiness Review questionnaire ([https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/NNNN-kep-template/README.md)|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/NNNN-kep-template/README.md)|smart-link]  section "Rollout,
   Upgrade and Rollback Planning" is marked as required for beta:

  ▎ "This section must be completed when targeting beta to a release."

  It explicitly asks:

  ▎ "Were upgrade and rollback tested? Was the upgrade->downgrade->upgrade path tested? Describe manual testing that was done and the outcomes."

  This is the basis for this story. The results of this manual testing will be documented in the KEP README.md under the PRR answer for this question.

  *Test procedure*

  On any Kubernetes cluster (v1.37+), perform the following steps and document the outcomes:

  Step 1 — Upgrade (enable feature):

* Start the cluster with PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime=true
* Create a PVC, verify Unused=True condition appears
* Create a Pod using the PVC, verify condition transitions to Unused=False
* Delete the Pod, verify condition transitions back to Unused=True

  Step 2 — Downgrade (disable feature):

* Restart kube-controller-manager and kube-apiserver with PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime=false
* Verify existing Unused condition on PVCs remains in etcd (not stripped)
* Verify condition stops being updated — create and delete a new Pod referencing the PVC, confirm condition does not change
* Verify Pods and PVCs continue to function normally (no disruption to workloads)

  Step 3 — Re-upgrade (re-enable feature):

* Restart components with PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime=true
* Verify condition updates resume on next PVC transition
* Create a Pod, verify Unused=False is set
* Delete the Pod, verify Unused=True is set with updated lastTransitionTime

  *Deliverable*

  Update the KEP README.md PRR answer with the actual test outcomes, replacing the current placeholder. Format should follow KEP-3751's style: numbered steps with
  observed behavior and any error messages encountered.

  *Acceptance Criteria:*

* All three phases (enable → disable → re-enable) tested on a Kubernetes cluster
* No disruption to existing Pods/PVCs during gate toggle 
* Condition correctly stops/resumes updating 
* Results documented in KEP README.md PRR section

* Create a Pod, verify Unused=False is set
* Delete the Pod, verify Unused=True is set with updated lastTransitionTime

items.toString:
Review the cloud platforms that kOps supports and update their CSI driver deployments to enable SELinuxMount.

For each platform:

# Set {{SELinuxMount: true}} in the CSIDriver object.
# Add hostpath mounts described in the [KEP|https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/1710-selinux-relabeling#csi-driver-considerations] to the node DaemonSet to ensure {{-o context}} actually works.

Specific platforms:

* *GCP PD*: kOps has [its own yaml files|https://github.com/kubernetes/kops/tree/5449914cfbe330e60fc8640e5ca06efd7f397a4f/upup/models/cloudup/resources/addons/gcp-pd-csi-driver.addons.k8s.io]. Already enabled via https://github.com/kubernetes/kops/commit/08d494ab7d823fdbeb95ab794d850060fa08c2ca. Ensure it survives future syncs from the CSI driver repo.
* *AWS EBS*: kOps [syncs|https://github.com/kubernetes/kops/tree/5449914cfbe330e60fc8640e5ca06efd7f397a4f/upup/models/cloudup/resources/addons/aws-ebs-csi-driver.addons.k8s.io] from upstream helm charts — SELinux support should be in the helm charts themselves.
* *AzureDisk*: kOps has [a sync script|https://github.com/kubernetes/kops/tree/5449914cfbe330e60fc8640e5ca06efd7f397a4f/upup/models/cloudup/resources/addons/azuredisk-csi-driver.addons.k8s.io] from upstream helm charts — SELinux support should be in the helm charts themselves.

Sync with kOps maintainers — Azure and maybe OpenStack could be enough since we can test there. We can't test the other clouds that kOps supports.
